meta.name: providers
meta.description: Every paid service the system calls, one description each (jav/core/providers.py). `key`: the key it needs, read from the environment (`typesafe`: TypeSafeJAV_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_API_KEY; `openai`: OPENAI_API_KEY; `azure_di`: AZURE_DI_ENDPOINT and AZURE_DI_KEY). `budget`: the provider whose budget its calls reserve from; the call log keeps the provider's own name. `enabled`: whether an installation may call it at all; an installation overrides it with JAV_PROVIDERS_ON / JAV_PROVIDERS_OFF (comma-separated provider names), and `off_note` says why it is off by default; `off_reason` names that reason as a code the screens show (`under_measurement`: being measured before an installation may choose it), while an installation's own switch reads as `switched_off`. `label`: its name on screen and in reports. (Glossary: Provider registry.)

changelog.note: Azure DI's `key_fallback` removed (the owner's decision of 2026-11-02: the framework works on its own, without the legacy project): Azure is reached only directly, with this installation's own endpoint and key, so a measurement with an Azure budget and no key says so like any other provider; an installation that switches it off (JAV_PROVIDERS_OFF=azure_di) is never sent anything.

OpenAI Decisions switched on (the owner's decision of 2026-11-02, after its measurement and the comparison with JEV on the same golden sets: selectable, not the default; it runs with JEV's bands). Its off_note and off_reason go; an installation still switches it off with JAV_PROVIDERS_OFF.
OpenAI Decisions' `off_reason`: under_measurement, so the screens show it greyed as under measurement (the owner's decision of 2026-11-01) instead of switched off; no other value changes.

Azure DI's `key_fallback`: without its own key it is reached through the legacy sidecar (for the PDFs under the legacy data folder), so a measurement does not say that every Azure call would be refused; no other value changes.

First version: JEV, OpenAI, OpenAI Decisions (OpenAI's judgement service; it spends from the OpenAI budget, the owner's decision of 2026-11-01, and is off until its measurement and the owner's decision) and Azure DI.
